Although Apple's annual September iPhone launch event is still about two months away, this year's situation will be different. In September, Apple will not roll out the entire iPhone lineup all at once, but will instead only debut the iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, and a brand-new foldable iPhone.

The iPhone Lineup Keeps Expanding

Over the past few years, the iPhone lineup has been steadily growing. Not long ago, only three new models were released each year: the iPhone 11, iPhone 11 Pro, and iPhone 11 Pro Max. By 2020, with the addition of the iPhone 12 mini, the number of models per year increased to four. In 2022, the iPhone 12 mini was replaced by the iPhone 14 Plus, which was later succeeded by the iPhone Air.

With the introduction of the iPhone 16e, the lineup has now grown to five models per year. Once the iPhone Ultra arrives, Apple's annual iPhone lineup will expand to six. With that many models, trying to launch them all at once would certainly make for a very crowded stage.

Therefore, Apple has decided to adopt a staggered rollout strategy.

Two iPhone Launch Events: Fall and Spring

The iPhone 18 series will consist of six models: iPhone 18, iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, iPhone 18e, iPhone Air 2, and iPhone Ultra.

The logic behind this staggered strategy is clear: flagship models debut in the fall, while mid-range and entry-level models arrive in the spring. The specific schedule is as follows:

  • Fall 2026: iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max, iPhone Ultra
  • Spring 2027: iPhone 18, iPhone 18e, iPhone Air 2

Whenever the iPhone lineup has expanded to four models, that extra model has consistently performed poorly in sales—whether it's the iPhone mini or the iPhone Plus. So Apple believes it's entirely reasonable to clearly separate the lineup and give that extra model its own moment in the spotlight.

However, the situation with the iPhone 18 will be slightly different. Reports indicate that Apple is working to unify the production processes for the iPhone 18 and iPhone 18e, so the differences between the two phones may be significantly narrowed.

It's still unclear whether this means the iPhone 18e will receive a major upgrade, or whether the iPhone 18 will be scaled down—but ultimately, the line between the two phones may come down to subtle distinctions in details like the display panel and camera.

Key Takeaways

In summary, assuming the iPhone Air isn't eventually discontinued (which I sincerely hope won't happen)—this is the new shape of the iPhone lineup going forward. Three in the fall, three in the spring. The ultimate goal is to allow Apple to better stagger its product launches and put the right device into the hands of the right consumers.

Another likely outcome is that the average selling price of iPhones will rise, since any consumer wanting to jump on the latest hardware craze will inevitably have to buy an iPhone 18 Pro, rather than a cheaper model.

Whether this staggered strategy can truly drive sales across all models remains to be seen, but these are some of my initial thoughts.

What are your thoughts on Apple's staggered iPhone strategy? Do you buy a new iPhone in the fall, or do you wait until spring? Feel free to share your opinions in the comments section.
